title: Escape the Spreading Fire
summary: Given a grid representing a field with grass, fire, and walls, you start at the top-left and aim to reach the bottom-right safehouse.
statement: Given a grid representing a field with grass, fire, and walls, you start at the top-left and aim to reach the bottom-right safehouse. Every minute, you can move to an adjacent grass cell, and fire spreads to adjacent non-wall cells. Determine the maximum number of minutes you can stay in your initial position before moving while still safely reaching the safehouse. If it's impossible, return -1. If you can always reach the safehouse regardless of the minutes stayed, return 10^9. A cell is adjacent if it touches the side of another cell.
constraints: Grid values are zero for grass, one for initial fire, and two for walls; start and safehouse are grass.
After each person move, fire spreads one step; entering the safehouse at the same minute as fire is allowed, but ties elsewhere are unsafe.
Return the maximum initial wait, -1 if escape is impossible immediately, or 1,000,000,000 if waiting is unbounded.
hints: First compute the earliest fire-arrival minute for every non-wall cell with multi-source BFS.
For a chosen wait, BFS the person using strict arrival before fire except non-strict arrival at the safehouse.
Check immediate escape, unbounded wait, then binary-search the greatest feasible wait.
Fire times are fixed independent of the person, feasibility is monotone in waiting time, and the BFS enforces the exact move-before-spread timing.
editorial: Fire times are fixed independent of the person, feasibility is monotone in waiting time, and the BFS enforces the exact move-before-spread timing.

tests.explanation: Waiting three minutes is feasible, while a fourth minute makes every safe route too late.
Walls isolate the fire from the only route, so the wait is unbounded.
